title: Feeling scared to take an HIV test
answer: It is very normal to feel afraid of an HIV test. Many people worry about the result or what others will think. Remember that knowing your status is a way of caring for yourself. If the result is negative, you can stay protected. If it is positive, free treatment lets you stay healthy, and starting early is best. You can bring a trusted friend or adult, and counsellors are there to support you.

answer: PrEP is medicine taken by HIV-negative people to prevent HIV. A health worker will talk with you to see if PrEP is right for you.

answer: Most people take PrEP without problems. Some feel mild side effects in the first weeks, such as nausea, stomach upset, headache or tiredness, which usually go away on their own. title: Difference between PrEP and PEP
answer: PrEP means 'before exposure': HIV-negative people at ongoing risk take it regularly to prevent HIV. PEP means 'after exposure': it is an emergency medicine started within 72 hours after a possible HIV exposure, such as a broken condom or rape, and taken for 28 days. If you often need PEP, ask a health worker about PrEP.
